Author: Siddharth
Bench: Siddharth
HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Court No. - 80 Case :- CRIMINAL APPEAL No. - 6925 of 2022 Appellant :- Jai Prakash Mishra Alias Chhotkau

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Respondent :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Appellant :- Rameshwar Prasad Mishra Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Dhirendra Kumar Srivastava Hon'ble Siddharth,J.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant; learned AGA for opposite party no.1; learned counsel for opposite party no.2 and perused the material placed on record.

The present criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been filed by the appellant to set aside the impugned order dated 23.6.2022 whereby the Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Prayagraj, has rejected the bail application of the appellant moved by him in Case Crime No. 73 of 2022, under Sections 366, 376, 504, 506, 120-B IPC and Section 3(1)(DA)/(DHA) SC/ST Act, Police Station Khiri, District Prayagraj.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: There is allegation against the appellant of abduction, rape, threatening and hatching conspiracy against a girl, belonging to scheduled caste.
Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that victim has claimed that the appellant befriended her on the false promise of marriage.
He took her to different places and committed the offence of rape.
Later accused did not married her and dropped her to her house.
He has submitted that it is a case of false implication on the basis of village politics.
Jai Prakash Mishra Alias Chhotkau vs State Of U.P. And Another on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175997433/

entities.text: Jai Prakash Mishra Alias Chhotkau vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 and learned AGA have vehemently opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant.
Learned counsel for opposite part no.2 has submitted that the appellant has not pleaded that there was any consenting relationship with the victim and therefore no offence is made out against him.
He has only submitted that it is a case of false implication of the appellant without giving any explanation of the same.
This Court after hearing the learned counsels for the parties does not finds any ground for enla rging the applicant on bail at this stage.
Criminal Appeal is accordingly dismissed.

The court below is directed to conclude the trial against the applicant, as expeditiously as possible,
preferably within a period of one year.
The Registrar (Compliance) of this Court is directed to communicate this order to the court concerned forthwith.
Order Date :- 20.4.2023/Ruchi Agrahari  Jai Prakash Mishra Alias Chhotkau vs State Of U.P.
